title: Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
abstract: We investigate timelike entanglement in quantum field theory using spacetime density matrices and provide a microscopic lattice realization. For a two-dimensional free real scalar field, we extend Gaussian diagonalization methods to the generally non-Hermitian reduced spacetime density matrix and determine its complete nonzero spectrum in the generic regular case, together with all integer Rényi moments. The real-time replica construction identifies these moments with Lorentzian branch-point twist-operator correlation functions. We test this identification against the full four-point function on a circle, boundary two-point functions with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and massive form-factor predictions, finding quantitative agreement in both magnitude and phase across distinct causal regimes. The boundary setup exhibits a finite causally connected window in which every integer Rényi entropy is real, showing that reality is not equivalent to causal disconnection. These results provide a microscopic lattice foundation for timelike entanglement and for Lorentzian twist-operator methods beyond equal-time regions.
summary: This work establishes a lattice realization for quantifying timelike entanglement in QFT using spacetime density matrices. By analyzing the spectrum of the reduced density matrix, the authors show that entanglement entropy moments precisely match predictions from Lorentzian twist-operator correlation functions. This provides a powerful, microscopic tool for studying quantum correlations across time separations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the concept of timelike entanglement in Quantum Field Theory (QFT) by analyzing reduced spacetime density matrices, extending entanglement measures beyond standard equal-time spatial cuts.
main_result: The authors provide a microscopic lattice realization for timelike entanglement, showing that Rényi entropy moments derived from the reduced density matrix match Lorentzian twist-operator correlation functions, even in regimes where reality is not guaranteed by causal disconnection.
method: The analysis uses Gaussian diagonalization techniques applied to the generally non-Hermitian reduced spacetime density matrix, determining its spectrum via a characteristic polynomial, and relating its moments to correlation functions using the real-time replica construction.
model_or_system: The study is performed on a free real scalar field, modeled on a lattice of coupled harmonic oscillators. The formalism is extended to analyze boundary effects (Periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann) and massive integrable QFTs.
key_observables: Reduced spacetime density matrix ($T_{A_0 B_t}$), Rényi entropy ($S_n$), von Neumann entropy ($S$), and Lorentzian twist-operator correlation functions (four-point and two-point functions).
important_parameters: Time separation ($t$), lattice size ($L$), mass scale ($\xi \sim m^{-1}$), and boundary conditions (DD, NN, PBC).
main_assumptions: The analysis is initially restricted to the vacuum state of a free scalar field, and the methods rely on extending Gaussian diagonalization to non-Hermitian operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup for the reduced density matrix on a circle and a strip, and show the evolution of Rényi entropies for various boundary conditions (DD, NN, DN) as a function of time separation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the reduced spacetime density matrix, calculating its spectrum and Rényi moments, establishing the connection to Lorentzian twist-operator correlators, and finally testing this identification against various boundary conditions and limits.
why_interesting: The rigorous lattice foundation for timelike entanglement provides a concrete, computable framework for understanding non-local quantum correlations in time, which is crucial for understanding dynamics in open or time-dependent quantum systems.
